title: Pick at random among the best
statement: In an adaptive test, pick at random among the few most informative items, not always the single best, or a fixed starting estimate gives every session the same opening.
example: Selection from one fixed starting estimate gave the same first passage in 100% of simulated sessions.
detail: The first run of a reading assessment on its production selection path found the first passage identical in 100% of sessions, because selection ran deterministically from one fixed session-start estimate, and flagged it as an exposure and security issue (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`). The engine then chose at random among the five most informative candidates in both selection phases, a procedure from published work on item selection, and the package records the finding as fixed (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/05_LIMITATIONS.md`). A later fix to the opening selection widened the distinct opening passages from 2 to 15 per 30 sessions (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_RESPONSE.md`).
against: The counts come from different stages: the 100% figure is from the first production-path run, and the widening from 2 to 15 came from a later, separate fix to the opening selection, so how many distinct openings random choice among the top five gave on its own isn't counted.

evidence.quote: - **(a) Deterministic first passage.** Production selection is deterministic from the fixed session-start prior — the first passage is identical in 100% of sessions, an exposure/security issue. Fix queued: randomize among near-optimal first passages.
selection among the top-5 information-ranked candidates, applied in both the quota-filling phase and the precision-extension phase (items 41–43)
The v1 deterministic-first-passage finding is **fixed** by randomesque selection
that widened distinct opening passages from 2 to 15 per 30 sessions

citations.ref: Procedures for selecting items for computerized adaptive tests (Applied Measurement in Education 2:4, 1989)
